Variance Components with Standard Errors and Confidence Intervals

Source: R/varcomp.R
varcomp.Rd

The variance components of a fitted model, with standard errors and confidence intervals, for every model class that predictmeans handles: the random-effect variances and covariances and the residual variance of lmer, lme and glmmTMB models (also with correlation and variance structures and random slopes), the random-effect (co)variances of glmer models, the correlation and variance-function parameters of gls and lme models, the stratum variance components of aov models with Error(), the smoothing variance components of mgcv::gam models and semireg fits, and the error term of lm, aov and glm models (residual variance, dispersion, or the negative binomial \(\theta\)).

Usage

varcomp(model, ci = TRUE, level = 0.95, ci_method = c("Satterthwaite", "Wald", "profile"),
        information = c("observed", "average", "expected"))

Arguments

model

A fitted model (see Description).

ci

TRUE (the default): add confidence intervals.

level

Confidence level of the intervals; the default is 0.95.

ci_method

How the intervals of variances are made: "Satterthwaite" (the default) chi-square intervals with \(\nu = 2 (estimate/SE)^2\) df, as SAS PROC MIXED (COVTEST CL); "Wald" Wald intervals on the log scale; "profile" (lmer, glmer) lme4's profile-likelihood intervals, which for a REML fit are those of the ML fit (lme4 profiles the ML deviance), so they do not go with the REML estimates. The other components always get the Wald intervals of the Details.

information

For REML fits of lmer, lme and gls models: the information matrix of the variance parameters behind the SEs: "observed" (the default, as SAS PROC MIXED), "average" (the average information of Genstat's and ASReml's REML: Genstat's s.e.) or "expected"; the same choices as for the Kenward-Roger df (df_method of predictmeans). Other fits use the observed information.

Value

A data frame with one row per component (random-effect variances and covariances by group, named group.term and group.term1.term2; correlation and variance-function parameters named cor.name and var.name; residual) and columns vcov (the estimate), SE and, with ci = TRUE, the limits. Values are rounded to 4 decimals; attribute "ci_method" says how the intervals were made.

Details

Standard errors are from the observed information of the variance parameters (the inverse Hessian of the REML, or ML, deviance at the estimates, as SAS PROC MIXED and the Kenward-Roger df of predictmeans), carried to the variance components by the delta method: lmer from the deviance in (theta, sigma), glmer from the Hessian lme4 stores for (theta, beta) (nAGQ = 0 fits: the deviance in theta), lme and gls from the REML (ML) log-likelihood in their unconstrained modelStruct parameters (any pdMat, corStruct and varFunc), glmmTMB from vcov(full = TRUE).

Intervals of variances: Satterthwaite's chi-square interval \([\nu \hat\sigma^2/\chi^2_{\nu, 1-\alpha/2}, \nu \hat\sigma^2/\chi^2_{\nu, \alpha/2}]\) with \(\nu = 2 (\hat\sigma^2/SE)^2\) (positive and skewed as the sampling distribution of a variance; for the residual variance of an lm it is the exact interval, \(\nu\) the residual df; for the stratum components of an aov Satterthwaite's interval from the mean squares). Other components: Wald intervals on the scale where the parameter is unbounded: atanh for correlations (a covariance: the interval of its correlation times the two SDs), log for other positive parameters (varIdent ratios, ranges, \(\theta\)), and the natural scale otherwise (e.g. the power of varPower). A variance estimated at its bound, zero, has no SE (the interval is (0, NA)), as SAS prints it; an analysis of variance estimate can be negative.

lm, aov, gaussian glm: the residual variance \(s^2\) with SE \(s^2 \sqrt{2/df}\) and the exact chi-square interval. Other glm families with an estimated dispersion (Gamma, inverse gaussian, quasi): the Pearson dispersion, with the same (approximate) SE and interval. Poisson and binomial: the dispersion is fixed at 1 (no SE). Negative binomial (MASS::glm.nb): \(\theta\) with its SE.

aov with Error(): the analysis of variance (method of moments) estimates of the variance of each error stratum, from the stratum mean squares and their expectations (as Genstat's stratum variances; they equal the REML estimates in balanced designs when positive, and can be negative), with SEs from \(var(MS) = 2 MS^2/df\) and Satterthwaite's chi-square intervals; with missing values, those of the design completed as in predictmeans.

gam: mgcv::gam.vcomp() (variances of the smooths, and the scale), its intervals squared, and the SEs from their width on the log scale; it needs method = "REML" or "ML".

Author

Dongwen Luo, Siva Ganesh and John Koolaard

Examples

library(predictmeans)
Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro*Variety+(1|Block/Variety), data=Oats)
varcomp(fm)
#>                               vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 %
#> Variety:Block.(Intercept) 106.0618  67.8754  40.9773  657.7703
#> Block.(Intercept)         214.4810 168.8381  70.8628 2575.3156
#> residual                  177.0831  37.3324 121.8272  280.9241
fm1 <- lme(yield ~ nitro*Variety, random=~1|Block/Variety, data=Oats)
varcomp(fm1)
#>                         vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 %
#> Block.(Intercept)   214.4745 168.8318  70.8610 2575.1691
#> Variety.(Intercept) 106.0618  67.8756  40.9772  657.7745
#> residual            177.0835  37.3325 121.8275  280.9250
# the same components by the analysis of variance
varcomp(aov(yield ~ nitro*Variety + Error(Block/Variety), data=Oats))
#>                   vcov       SE    2.5 %    97.5 %
#> Block         214.4771 168.8340  70.8619 2575.2100
#> Block:Variety 106.0618  67.8755  40.9773  657.7726
#> residual      177.0833  37.3324 121.8274  280.9246

data(Orthodont, package="nlme")
mod1 <- lme(distance ~ age, random=~age|Subject, data=Orthodont)
varcomp(mod1)
#>                            vcov     SE   2.5 %   97.5 %
#> Subject.(Intercept)      5.4151 4.9583  1.5819 128.6996
#> Subject.age.(Intercept) -0.3211 0.4244 -0.4943   0.1570
#> Subject.age              0.0513 0.0415  0.0166   0.6844
#> residual                 1.7162 0.3303  1.2163   2.6042
# correlation and variance structures
mod2 <- gls(distance ~ age*Sex, correlation=corAR1(form=~1|Subject),
            weights=varIdent(form=~1|Sex), data=Orthodont)
varcomp(mod2)
#>              vcov     SE  2.5 %  97.5 %
#> cor.Phi    0.7473 0.0681 0.5815  0.8535
#> var.Female 0.5647 0.0908 0.4121  0.7738
#> residual   9.5035 2.8443 5.7032 18.9234
# the error term of a linear model
varcomp(lm(yield ~ Block + nitro*Variety, data=Oats))
#>              vcov      SE    2.5 %   97.5 %
#> residual 254.2192 48.4777 180.6923 384.1423
